title: Introduce Trace Gatekeeper and metric provenance cleanup to reduce cardinality and latency
creator: Maya Patel
description: We need a small, centralized "Trace Gatekeeper" component in the runtime to apply deterministic sampling, provenance tagging, and attribute canonicalization. Current flow leaves high-cardinality attributes unsanitized across services (user-generated metadata, ephemeral container ids) which increases metrics costs and explodes cardinality in downstream TSDBs. The Gatekeeper will run inline in the hot path with a zero-copy-friendly API and an opt-in static whitelist per-service.
motivation: Reduce per-tenant metric/trace cardinality by ~60-80% and decrease tracing-related CPU/alloc overhead on the hot path. Make provenance of attributes explicit (runtime / agent / customer-prompt) to support targeted filters and audits. Remove duplicate remediation logic scattered across services.
success_metrics: 1) 60% reduction in unique label combinations per-hour across top 50 tenants within 4 weeks of rollout. 2) End-to-end trace path CPU reduced by 20% for hot-path requests (bench). 3) 90th percentile trace export latency < 150ms under 95th percentile load. 4) No customer-facing errors introduced; observability dashboards unchanged in basic coverage.
tasks: Design: finalize Gatekeeper interface and whitelist config format (config proto + local override).
Upgrade: bump OpenTelemetry SDK to v1.18.0 and switch to the new Resource detector API.
Implementation: add gatekeeper module in runtime/tracing with zero-copy attribute filter and provenance tagger.
Canonicalization: implement canonicalizers for container_id, user_id, and model_id with regex rules and length caps.
Sampler: implement deterministic hashed-sampling at tenant+route granularity and integrate with adaptive-sampling service.
Logging: standardize trace-level logs to structured lightweight codec (move from fmt->zap-lite path).
Bench: synthetic load test comparing before/after CPU, allocs, and export latency (scripts in infra/tests/trace-bench).
Rollout: staged canary by tenant percentage (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with automatic rollback trigger on error budget burn.
Docs: update runtime README, console docs for sampling controls and provenance fields.
PRs & review: open PRs and follow review feedback
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper deployed behind feature flag and enabled for internal test cluster.
Automated regression tests validate canonicalization rules and sampling determinism.
Bench results attached showing CPU and alloc reductions meeting success metrics.
Rollout playbook documented with rollback conditions and alerting thresholds.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout with percentage-based routing in Console. Monitor cardinality dashboard and trace export error rate. Automated rollback when trace export error rate increases >0.5% absolute or customer error budget burn >2% in 15m.
rollback_plan: Disable Gatekeeper via runtime feature flag; revert sampling config; hotfix release pipeline prepared (tags: hotfix/trace-gatekeeper).
risks: Incorrect canonicalization can under- or over-sanitize fields causing loss of needed context. Sampling changes may bias A/B experiments. Upgrade to OTEL v1.18 may introduce minor behavior deltas in resource semantics.
mitigations: Include a per-tenant opt-out and sample of raw attributes forwarded to warm-storage for first 24h after rollout.
Run A/B on traffic slices to detect bias against production signals.
Smoke test OTEL upgrade in staging with a full downstream exporter stack before prod upgrade.
